verdict.rationale: Bento documents alerts written in plain natural language that compile to trace queries and route to Slack, PagerDuty, email, or webhook. It also groups alert fires into incidents. It surfaces cost per run and tool failure rates as built-in metrics, but the evidence is FAQ and marketing-level only. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of threshold or spike alerts on cost and error rates, eval-score-drop alert conditions, in-depth alert configuration docs, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can set alerts on error rates, cost spikes, or eval-score drops and get notified in Slack, PagerDuty, or email

citations.quote: Alerts are defined in plain natural language... Rules compile to trace queries and route to Slack, PagerDuty, email, or webhook.
Write alerts in English. Bento groups fires into incidents and judges each one real or benign
you see cost per run, tool failure rates, drift over prompt versions, and regressions across deploys out of the box.
